name: Olive leaf extract (Olea europaea)
short: 12-week trial, 621 people on blood pressure treatment: oral olive leaf extract lowered blood pressure; glucose also fell. No significant adverse events. 31-person diabetes trial: no serious events.
text: In a 12-week multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 621 people being treated for high blood pressure, oral olive leaf extract lowered 24-hour blood pressure and was associated with a significant reduction in blood glucose, and no significant adverse events were reported; the abstract does not report low blood pressure or low blood sugar, list milder events or discuss interactions with blood pressure medicines. In a 24-week pilot placebo-controlled trial in 31 adults with type 2 diabetes not using insulin, the extract and placebo were both well tolerated, with no severe or serious adverse events in either group. These are two trials of modest length, and the abstracts do not describe the extracts' composition. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
